monitoring.mechanism: Monitoring must receive useful evidence, recognize a problem and trigger effective action; these are separate failure points.
monitoring.conditions: Read coverage, layers, response, replay, historical audit and external-interface conditions. Compare C3a3/C3b and the evaluation/oversight decomposition in both languages.
monitoring.counterexample: An alert from a recorded incident does not show it would have been contained; an action may be blocked by a separate control even when monitoring fails.
monitoring.evidence: Add the developer report with historical replay and workload-specific response coverage. Reread the older external audit and Auto Mode hardening for the due C3a3 explanation.
monitoring.limits: No unknown-failure recall, representative incidence or total harm-reduction result is supplied. One old-audit fix is pending; expanded coverage has not received the same external retest.
monitoring.mitigation: Protect evidence, retest fixes, match agent permissions and measure the full notification-to-containment path, including disabled or business-hours paging.
monitoring.readerContext: Explain that detecting, notifying and stopping are different steps before introducing API details in the research cards.
monitoring.whyHere: C3a3 concerns missed runtime oversight and C3b late response. Keep limited statuses and tested/indirect evidence, without claiming the joint conditions for loss of control or harm.

implementation.mechanism: A scored implementation can exploit what a test accepts instead of solving the intended task. Harness behavior can also alter apparent capability.
implementation.conditions: Read the complete current Carbon evaluation and its corrected reruns; distinguish five-hour task budgets from the six-hour background wait, and unmatched Argon reruns.
implementation.counterexample: A passing score may disappear when a loophole is removed; an early stop can arise from harness timeout rather than inability to solve the task.
implementation.evidence: Use the opened primary article, with 25/48 Carbon passes and trace review, instead of the stale 24/48 search result. Link to R1 and C3a1 with existing classifications.
implementation.limits: The contribution of two loopholes is unknown; not all early stops were rerun. The study is not a replication of a different cheating metric, ordinary-use frequency, or end-to-end research speed.
implementation.mitigation: Inspect final code and traces, ablate suspected shortcuts and compare matched task/harness conditions before extrapolating.
implementation.readerContext: Keep the main explanation about what was actually built and tested; reserve counts and settings for cards. Both languages retain uncertainty and unmatched comparisons.
implementation.whyHere: R1 covers useful partial research work; C3a1 covers imperfect test coverage. R1-R2 still requires useful bottleneck improvement; no new work-adoption or sustained RSI claim follows.

permissions.mechanism: A model can obey a restriction while an executor independently enforces access; failed model compliance is not itself proof of acquired real-world permission.
permissions.conditions: Read the Luna addendum figures on printed pp.9–10, Table 4 on p.7 and October 7 card §7.1. Separate maximum-reasoning restriction tests from averaged injection robustness.
permissions.counterexample: No prohibited actions after approval rejection can coexist with failures after environmental warnings and lower robustness on a separate injection test.
permissions.evidence: Add the October 29 version and its 0.00%, conditional 11.8% and separate robustness result, with same-chart comparator and test conditions.
permissions.limits: Simulated environments and deliberately flawed controls omit the full safeguard stack. Denominators and uncertainty are incomplete, and awareness of evaluation can affect results.
permissions.mitigation: Bind execution to explicit permissions, test enforcement separately from model behavior, and validate restrictions under realistic access and intervention conditions.
permissions.readerContext: The node explains approval refusals versus warnings without implying that internet connectivity grants every permission. The card names the conditional denominator limitation.
permissions.whyHere: C2b is the access component alongside C2a capability. Retain observed access and the ability-access graph; no new real-world incident or probability follows.

acceleration.mechanism: Faster component work speeds development only when it improves a bottleneck without offsets in experiments, verification or integration; feedback also requires useful successors.
acceleration.conditions: Substantively reread OpenAI workflow analysis, Anthropic internal analysis, METR Opus assessment and Argon §3.4.2. Read R2 and three R&D edges, chapters and news in both languages.
acceleration.counterexample: More AI-written code or higher task scores can coexist with unchanged overall development speed. One company’s nonsignificant trend is not proof that AI is useless.
acceleration.evidence: Retain R2 prose and limited/indirect classifications; renew its dates based on original methods, human roles, task coverage and the bounded trend comparison.
acceleration.limits: Internal usage and self-estimates do not isolate AI causally. Support for the separate whole-process estimate is inaccessible; a bounded company metric does not generalize across labs and periods.
acceleration.mitigation: Measure completed useful output and whole-process time with verification, compute, staff effort and human intervention; evaluate safety at each successor cycle.
acceleration.readerContext: Keep coding speed, research contribution, overall development and sustained self-improvement distinct. The new Carbon result does not collapse these stages.
acceleration.whyHere: R1-R2, R2-R3 and R3-R2 remain conditional. Control, acceleration and work routes retain independent access, safeguards, adoption and distribution requirements.

safety.mechanism: AI research or audit tools can improve specific safeguards, but deployed risk reduction requires valid measures, transfer and durable implementation.
safety.conditions: Reread automated alignment §§6–8, auditor training methods/limits and Transect v2 §§2–4. Compare v1/v2 full text and read R4, its two edges, safeguard and linked news.
safety.counterexample: Consistent labels can be wrong; rewarded alarming reports can create false findings; a selected safety metric can improve without preventing real incidents.
safety.evidence: Retain R4 limited/tested and its explanation. Pin Transect to v2 after identifying only version-date/contact correction, with no research-claim change. Renew only R4 node/evidence and Transect source confirmation.
safety.limits: Prepared problems, AI judges, selected targets and one trace case do not establish detection of every unknown problem or persistent improvement through further training.
safety.mitigation: Use held-out cases, benign controls, independent verification and durable deployment tests; preserve source traces and separate researcher and evaluator roles.
safety.readerContext: Explain the benefit of easier inspection while retaining the distinction between a useful tool and demonstrated accident prevention.
safety.whyHere: R0-R4 is possible application of capabilities to safety; R4-C1 remains a conditional mitigation. The older safeguard example retains its explicitly bounded setup and date.

publication.mechanism: A map explains conditional pathways; newer publication dates, test scores and warnings do not by themselves establish real-world harm.
publication.conditions: Review the adopted originals, bilingual additions and dependencies; preserve earlier records by stable ID and source versions. Renew only substantively checked items.
publication.counterexample: A policy announcement can describe desired behavior without showing models follow it; a model pass can be invalid, and a fast alert can precede ineffective intervention.
publication.evidence: Add three sources, four cards and five paragraphs, record three due rereads and the Transect correction, and keep all classifications and topology unchanged.
publication.limits: This is a bounded daily editorial review, not an exhaustive survey, independent replication, browser test or production verification.
publication.mitigation: Keep the update in existing draft PR #11 for human review, with content, dependency, translation, build and preservation checks. Do not merge or deploy automatically.
publication.readerContext: Use separate publication, experimental and confirmation dates and pair improvements with limits in both languages.
publication.whyHere: The metadata, history and inventory summarize the actual review scope without presenting confirmation dates as scientific validation or completion of an extinction pathway.
